Takeda R&D President Andy Plump and GV Managing Partner Krishna Yeshwant Announce Retirements

by GOAI
Share To
FacebookTwitterLinkedInCopy Link
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:01
Instaread

Takeda Pharmaceutical Company’s President of Research and Development, Andy Plump, and GV’s Managing Partner, Krishna Yeshwant, have announced their respective plans to retire. Both executives confirmed their departures this week, marking a significant leadership transition for the pharmaceutical and venture capital sectors.

Andy Plump concludes a tenure at Takeda during which he oversaw the company’s transition into a global research-driven organization. His leadership focused on restructuring the firm’s R&D pipeline and expanding its international presence. Simultaneously, Krishna Yeshwant prepares to step down from his role at GV, the venture capital arm of Alphabet Inc. Yeshwant managed a diverse portfolio of investments, contributing to the firm’s strategy in the life sciences and technology markets. Both organizations have begun the process of identifying successors to fill these leadership positions.

Wendy Short Bartie Integrates Patient Advocacy and Public Trust into Bristol Myers Squibb Business Strategy

by GOAI
Share To
Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Copy Link

Wendy Short Bartie of Bristol Myers Squibb is repositioning corporate affairs as a central driver of enterprise value by integrating patient advocacy, public trust, and healthcare access into the company’s core business strategy. This approach treats corporate reputation as a form of currency that directly influences the organization’s operational success and its ability to engage with the broader healthcare ecosystem.

By aligning corporate communications and external relations with patient-centered outcomes, Bartie aims to bridge the gap between internal corporate objectives and the needs of the communities the company serves. This strategy emphasizes that maintaining a strong reputation requires consistent engagement with patient voices and a transparent commitment to improving access to medical treatments. Through this framework, the company seeks to demonstrate how institutional trust functions as a measurable asset that supports long-term growth and stability within the pharmaceutical industry.

Shine Spect USA Updates Clinical and Safety Guidelines for Xenon Xe-133 Gas

by GOAI
Share To
Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Copy Link

Shine Spect USA, LLC updated the product information for Xenon Xe-133 gas on September 11, 2026. The updated documentation provides clinical and technical specifications for the radioactive diagnostic agent, which medical professionals use primarily for pulmonary ventilation studies and blood flow measurements.

The updated filing outlines the chemical properties, clinical pharmacology, and administration guidelines for the gas. It details the necessary safety protocols for handling the radioactive material, including dosage recommendations and contraindications for patient use. The document also specifies the physical characteristics of the isotope and the required storage conditions to maintain the stability of the product. These guidelines serve as the official reference for healthcare providers regarding the clinical application and safety requirements of Xenon Xe-133.

Amorepacific Updates Hera Black Cushion Ingredient Disclosures for Ten Foundation Shades

by GOAI
Share To
Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Copy Link

Amorepacific Corporation has updated the product information for its Hera Black Cushion foundation line, confirming the inclusion of octinoxate, titanium dioxide, and zinc oxide across ten specific shades. The updated filing, dated September 11, 2026, details the chemical composition for the foundation series, which serves as a lotion-based cosmetic product.

The affected shades include 13N1, 17N1, 17C2, 19N1, 21N1, 21C2, 21W1, 22N1, 26N1, and 26W1. According to the documentation provided to the DailyMed database, these active ingredients are utilized across the entire range of the Hera Black Cushion collection. The company maintains these records to provide transparency regarding the formulation of its cosmetic offerings.

AvKARE Updates Prescribing Information for Etonogestrel and Ethinyl Estradiol Vaginal Ring

by GOAI
Share To
Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Copy Link

AvKARE has released updated prescribing information for the etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol vaginal ring, a hormonal contraceptive device. The updated documentation, published on September 11, 2026, outlines the clinical specifications, usage instructions, and safety profile for the product as registered in the DailyMed database.

The updated filing details the pharmacological composition of the ring, which releases a combination of the progestin etonogestrel and the estrogen ethinyl estradiol to prevent pregnancy. The documentation provides comprehensive guidance on the insertion and removal process, the recommended duration of use, and the management of potential side effects. It also includes clinical data regarding contraindications, drug interactions, and warnings for patients with specific medical histories. Healthcare providers and patients can access the full technical specifications and regulatory information through the National Library of Medicine’s DailyMed portal.

Life science companies and a record number of investors gathered at NLS Days 2026 to present research data, establish business partnerships, and secure capital. The event served as a platform for stakeholders to engage in dealmaking activities within the Nordic life sciences sector.

Participants utilized the conference to showcase clinical and scientific findings while facilitating discussions regarding potential collaborations. The high turnout of investors marked a notable increase in attendance compared to previous years, reflecting current engagement levels in the regional market. These interactions focused on the exchange of information between emerging firms and financial backers to support ongoing development and funding initiatives.
